evidence: Clear directory-based modularity with logical separation into models, services, utils, tests, and core modules (e.g., config, logger, constants)
Services (e.g., OrderService, PriceService, AccountService) are cohesive, stateful components with well-defined responsibilities, but all reside in a single deployable unit (package)
No inter-process communication or network boundaries observed; all services import and call each other directly via Python imports
AlphaSquaredTrader and EnhancedRESTClient act as orchestrators/composers, not as independent services
Shared domain models (Order, Product) and cross-cutting concerns (logging, config) are centralized in the same module
Repository depth is shallow (max 3), typical of well-organized monoliths rather than distributed systems
Test structure mirrors production structure (tests/ mirrors coinbase_advanced_trader/), indicating tight coupling between components
risks: Tight coupling between services (e.g., EnhancedRESTClient imports multiple services directly) may reduce testability and flexibility over time
No explicit ports/adapters boundary detected, making it harder to swap external integrations (e.g., REST client) without affecting core logic
Monolithic deployment may limit scalability and independent evolution of components as the system grows
